concepts.name: Reading kiln temperature by glow color (pre-cone judgment)
concepts.open_problem: Skilled firers historically judged kiln heat purely by the color of light through peep/bung holes (red->yellow->white); this perceptual mapping of incandescent color to maturation state is tacit, lighting-dependent and still used as a backup when instruments fail.
concepts.app_market_check: none seen (AI kiln work targets automated temp control/kiln-packing, not visual color-reading by a human; e.g. Aberystwyth/Parkinson-Spencer kiln-packing ML, generic 'AI-driven kiln' temp control)
concepts.verbatim_quote: Skilled kiln tradespeople would have to judge the heat by the color of the light emanating from holes in the kiln called bung holes (referred to as peep holes in the USA for obvious reasons). As the temperature in the kiln rose, the color would move from red to yellow to white.

concepts.name: Reading pyrometric cone bend as 'heat work' not temperature
concepts.open_problem: Cones integrate time+temperature ('heat work') into a physical slump; the firer must interpret the degree/angle of cone bend to know when a glaze/body has truly matured, a judgment temperature instruments alone cannot give.
concepts.app_market_check: none seen (no shipping consumer app reads cone deformation; firing-chart reference sites only)
concepts.verbatim_quote: Cones measure 'heat work' which is the combined effect of time and temperature, and clay and glazes are formulated to mature when a certain amount of heat work is achieved.

concepts.name: Judging reduction atmosphere by flame and smell
concepts.open_problem: Without an oxygen analyzer, potters judge whether the kiln is in oxygen-stealing reduction by watching the flame at the peep holes and smelling unburned fuel, then adjusting burners/damper - a multisensory real-time judgment of combustion chemistry.
concepts.app_market_check: none seen (oxygen probes exist as hardware, but no app replicates the flame/smell judgment)
concepts.verbatim_quote: Reduction is difficult to judge and not everyone can afford an oxygen analyzer in the kiln.

concepts.name: Wood-firing stoking rhythm / ember-bed management (anagama)
concepts.open_problem: Anagama firing requires teams to judge when to stoke from the look of the pots inside, wetness of walls, ember-bed glow and airflow over multi-day firings; stoking rhythm is adjusted by feel to avoid over-stoking, an unquantified embodied skill.
concepts.app_market_check: none seen (a USPTO patent for an 'automated wood-fired kiln' exists as hardware, but no consumer app judges stoking rhythm)
concepts.verbatim_quote: Stoking occurs around the clock until a variety of variables are achieved including the way the fired pots look inside the kiln, the temperature reached and sustained, the amount of ash applied, the wetness of the walls and the pots.

concepts.name: Glaze-defect diagnosis preserving visual character (crazing/crawling)
concepts.open_problem: Correcting crazing/shivering/crawling while keeping a glaze's intended look is described as a classic ceramic-chemistry problem; it requires trade-off judgment across expansion, surface tension and application that resists simple automation.
concepts.app_market_check: none seen for the judgment; glaze-calc software (Glazy, digitalfire) assists chemistry but does not decide the aesthetic trade-off
concepts.verbatim_quote: Crazing appears as a network of fine, spidery cracks that can appear immediately after firing or sometime later.

concepts.name: Judging completion of lime/brick burning by flame cues
concepts.open_problem: In traditional clamp/kiln burning of lime, completion of calcination is read from the disappearance of a blue flame at the top - a perceptual end-point judgment over a multi-week burn with no instrument.
concepts.verbatim_quote: A blue flame at the top disappears indicates completion.

concepts.name: Lime mortar mix/slaking judgment (tacit, locally-tuned)
concepts.open_problem: The 'perfect mix' for a given situation and the slaking-to-application skill were never well quantified and varied by local materials, passed person-to-person; judging slaking readiness and mix character remains experiential and at risk of being lost.
concepts.app_market_check: none seen (premixed NHL products like Ecologic/Lancaster Lime Works sold, but no app judges slaking/mix readiness)
concepts.verbatim_quote: Despite its enduring utility over many centuries, lime mortar's effectiveness as a building material has not been well understood; time-honoured practices were based on tradition, folklore and trade knowledge, vindicated by the vast number of old buildings that remain standing.

concepts.name: Judging cob/earthen mix consistency by foot and feel
concepts.open_problem: Cob mix readiness is judged tactilely (feet sensing consistency, hand/rip tests for straw content); because no two soils are alike, judgment develops only from working the wet material, defying fixed recipes.
concepts.verbatim_quote: Traditionally, mixing was a process to be learned, with judgment developing out of working directly with the wet material, since the nature and requirements of the particular soil being prepared become apparent as mixing proceeds.

concepts.name: Dry-stone stone selection / fitting by eye
concepts.open_problem: A waller must choose each stone's seen face and fit stones without mortar largely by eye and trial-and-error, drawing on familiarity with regional stone; correct selection per position strongly affects wall lifetime but is not reducible to measurement.
concepts.app_market_check: none seen (some academic structural-soundness studies exist; no shipping consumer app picks/fits stones)
concepts.verbatim_quote: Selection of the correct stone for every position in the wall makes an enormous difference to the lifetime of the finished product, and a skilled waller will take time making the selection.

notes: Least AI-touched / most fertile (tacit sensory judgments with no consumer app): judging reduction atmosphere by flame+smell (none), anagama wood-fire stoking rhythm/ember-bed (none), judging lime/brick burn completion by blue-flame disappearance (none), lime mortar slaking+mix readiness (none), cob mix consistency by foot/feel (none). Calibration note: existing AI/ML in ceramics is real but aimed elsewhere - kiln-PACKING optimization (Aberystwyth/Parkinson-Spencer), automated temperature-control kilns, and pottery-documentation deep learning (PyPotteryLens) - NOT the human sensory firing judgments above, so those judgments stay none/very-low. Domain A (physics-bearing kiln/glaze) is the richer vein, consistent with learned HIGH-fertility flag for physics-bearing crafts.
